title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover memory manager + defrag scheduling tuning
author: Anita Desai
description: Motivation: KV cache spillover and defragmentation have been a persistent source of tail latency and occasional OOMs under mixed workloads. We observed increased paging during long-running conversational sessions and poor defrag scheduling causing repeated write amplification to spill devices. This PR introduces an adaptive spillover memory manager that reasons about fragmentation, hot-set locality, and recent access patterns to make eviction and paging decisions. It also tunes the defrag coordinator's scheduling heuristics to prioritize low-latency lanes and reduce background compaction contention with inference threads. Changes are behind a runtime flag (kv.adaptive_spillover_enabled) and include telemetry and feature gates for gradual rollout. Summary of changes: - New adaptive memory manager that: * tracks per-shard fragmentation score and hotness decay windows * estimates the cost of paging vs in-memory eviction and prefers incremental spill operations for large fragmented regions * allows soft-reservation for low-latency lanes to avoid defrag interference - Defrag coordinator updates: * defrag windows now consider in-flight request load and GPU kernel occupancy before starting heavy compaction * adaptive backoff when spill write throughput exceeds configured thresholds - Eviction policy changes: * hybrid LRU+LFU weighting to avoid evicting moderately hot tokens during bursty workloads * prioritized eviction of high-fragmentation segments to reduce subsequent paging - Metrics & tracing: * added kv.memory.fragmentation_score, kv.eviction.paged_bytes, kv.spill.write_latency histograms * added traces for spill decision path and defrag start/stop reasons - Tests & CI: * unit tests for fragmentation scoring and decision thresholds * integration test simulating sustained multi-session workloads with synthetic fragmentation patterns * load test harness update to capture end-to-end spill latency and GPU occupancy effects Rollout plan: feature off by default; staged rollout to canary Dedicated hosts for 48h, monitor kv.eviction.paged_bytes and inference tail latency, then enable in production if thresholds met. Related: ENG-3421 (kv cache stability), ENG-3478 (defrag coordinator refactor).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain the tradeoff used to decide between paging a fragmented region vs evicting entries? The PR notes an estimator but lacks the math.
Anita Desai: Added a short doc block in manager.h describing the cost model (expected spill bytes * backend_write_cost + estimated readback penalty vs eviction GSM). See manager.h lines 120-160.
Priya Kapoor: Defrag coordinator now checks GPU kernel occupancy — do we have a fallback if occupancy measurement is noisy on some cloud providers?
Anita Desai: Yes — coordinator falls back to conservative wall-clock thresholds when occupancy metrics are unavailable; added a test to assert this behavior.
Diego Alvarez: Integration load test is flaky in CI, failing occasionally on RPC timeouts. Can we increase timeouts or make the harness more resilient?
Anita Desai: Increased timeout in the harness and added a retry on transient RPCs. Also changed CI job to rerun flaky test once on failure.
release_notes: Improves KV cache memory management and spillover behavior: introduces adaptive spillover memory manager, hybrid eviction policy, and tuned defrag scheduling to reduce tail latency and paging. Metrics and tracing added for rollout monitoring.
perf_summary: Canary results: ~9-12% improvement in 99th percentile inference latency for mixed-conversation workloads, 18% reduction in spill write amplification, and ~70% fewer OOMs observed in limited canary. Read/write spill latency median improved from 24ms -> 18ms in our lab harness.
notes: Feature gate kv.adaptive_spillover_enabled controls rollout. Operators should monitor kv.eviction.paged_bytes and kv.memory.fragmentation_score when enabling. Default behavior unchanged until flag is enabled.
